meta.title: The Geography of Shermer
meta.status: Compiled list · not yet checked against production records, location permits or contemporaneous press
meta.note: In several Hughes films the fictional suburb of Shermer, Illinois acts as a composite of real Chicago-area places, especially Northbrook, Highland Park, Winnetka, Evanston, Glencoe, Skokie, Des Plaines and Wilmette. Shermer Road is a real road in Northbrook, and Glenbrook North High School sits at 2300 Shermer Road.

basis.dataset: Stated in the compiled location list.
basis.editorial: Added by the guide editors from general knowledge. Unconfirmed — verify before publication.

films.title: Sixteen Candles
films.note: One of the foundational films for the Hughes North Shore geography.
films.sig: A strong early example of the Hughes North Shore visual world: Evanston → Skokie → Highland Park → Glencoe.

films.title: The Breakfast Club
films.story: Almost entirely Shermer High School, fictional Shermer, Illinois
films.note: Shermer High is effectively a composite of multiple suburban schools.
films.sig: Shermer High can be read as one fictional destination with two primary real-world anchors: Des Plaines and Northbrook.

films.title: Weird Science
films.sig: Highland Park is essentially the residential center of the film.

films.title: Ferris Bueller’s Day Off
films.story: Shermer / North Shore suburbs plus downtown Chicago
films.note: Probably the richest single Hughes film for a Chicago location map: the plot explicitly connects suburbia to downtown. Also: various Loop and downtown streets.
films.sig: The clearest suburbs-to-city journey in the Hughes universe.

films.title: Planes, Trains and Automobiles
films.story: New York → the Midwest → the Chicago suburbs
films.note: Expands the map well beyond the North Shore.
films.sig: Pulls the cinematic world outward into greater Illinois and the Midwest.

films.title: She’s Having a Baby
films.note: Combines suburban life with recognizable downtown Chicago locations.
films.sig: Shows commuter-suburb life and Metra geography inside the Hughes universe.

films.title: Uncle Buck
films.note: One of the most geographically scattered North Shore Hughes films. Additional production around Northbrook, Skokie, Glencoe, Riverwoods and Northfield.
films.sig: Practically a tour of the northern suburbs.

films.title: Home Alone
films.note: One of the strongest Hughes-associated films for identifiable suburban geography.
films.sig: Creates an especially strong Winnetka / Hubbard Woods micro-map.

films.title: Curly Sue
films.note: Notably more urban than the classic Hughes teen films. Also: Loop and downtown street locations.
films.sig: Adds a downtown professional / office Chicago layer.

films.title: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York
films.note: Most of the story occurs in New York, but significant Chicago-area production belongs on a Hughes map.
films.sig: Distinguishes Chicago locations that are Chicago in the story from Chicago locations doubling for New York.

films.title: Dennis the Menace
films.note: Another very strong suburban Illinois film. Additional scenes in the Cook County Forest Preserve.
films.sig: Hinsdale brings the Hughes suburban aesthetic into the western suburbs.

films.title: Baby’s Day Out
films.note: A highly Chicago-centric film. Also: various downtown streets and buildings.
films.sig: Chicago itself effectively becomes the baby’s giant playground.

films.title: Home Alone 3
films.note: Later Hughes, but geographically very relevant.
films.sig: Adds another concentrated Evanston residential cluster.

films.title: National Lampoon’s Vacation
films.story: The Griswolds set out from suburban Chicago
films.note: Opening drive uses Chicago expressway and lakefront imagery; most of the production happened outside Illinois.
films.sig: A short Chicago prologue — Lake Shore Drive and the Dan Ryan — before the road trip leaves the map.

films.title: Pretty in Pink
films.note: Part of the broader Shermer-style suburban world, but primarily shot around Los Angeles. Placement here is a best guess.
films.sig: Plotted inside the Shermer composite on screen; annotated as a Los Angeles shoot.

films.title: National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation
films.note: Generally understood as a Chicago-area Griswold story; much of it was shot on California backlots. Placement is a best guess.
films.sig: A story-world suburb only — the house itself stands on a California backlot.

secondTier.title: Some Kind of Wonderful
secondTier.note: Hughes suburban tone, but not a strong actual Chicago filming-location candidate.

secondTier.title: Career Opportunities
secondTier.note: Feels very Hughes; primarily shot in Georgia.
